senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. כפף)to bend, arch over, cover; v. כְּפוֹר, כּוֹפֶר &c.
[to pass over with one’s palm &c., to wipe out, rub (cmp. חפף),] to deny, withhold the truth by claiming ignorance; to ignore (mostly with ב of the object).
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 4a:8">B. Mets. 4ᵃ</cite> <he>הכּוֹפֵר במלוה</he> he who denied having received a loan (and was refuted before being sworn, v. <cite ref="E00475"><he>הֶיסֵּת</he></cite>).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 4a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>על מה שכ׳ וכ׳</he> he is sworn on what he denied.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shevuot 4:1">Shebu. IV, 1</cite> <he>עד שיִכְפְּרוּ בהן בב״ד</he> until they declare their ignorance (of the testimony) before court.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shevuot 4:4">Ib. 4</cite> <he>כָּפְרוּ שניהן וכ׳</he> if both witnesses pleaded ignorance at the same time.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shevuot 4:4">Ib.</cite> <he>כָּפְרָה הראשונה</he> if the first set of witnesses pleaded ignorance. Ib. VI, 3 <he>והודה … וכ׳ בקרקעות</he> and defendant admits the debt concerning vessels, but denies it as to landed estate.
<cite ref="Shabbat 116a:8">Sabb. 116ᵃ</cite> <he>מכירין וכוֹפְרִין</he> they know (true religion) and yet are disbelievers.
Cant. R. to I, 14 (play on הכפר, ib.) שכ׳ באו״ה He disowned the gentiles (did not assist them), opp. הודה; a. v. fr.—כ׳ בעיקר to deny the principle of religion (unity of God &c.).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 39a">Snh. 39ᵃ</cite> <he>א״ל כּוֹפֵר</he> ed. (Ms. M. <cite ref="S01080"><he>קיסר</he></cite>) an infidel said &c.

senses.gloss: (v. כַּפָּרָה) to say of a person, ‘May his death be an atonement for his sins!’ euphem. for to be angry at.
units: <cite ref="Pesachim 69a:5">Pes. 69ᵃ</cite> <he>אל תַּכְפִּירֵנִי בשעת הדין</he> ed. (Ms. M. a. Ar. <he>תְּכַפְּרֵנִי</he>) do not make me an atonement (saying <he>תהא מיתתו כפרה</he>) at the time of judgment (differ. in comm.); <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 46b">Ab. Zar. 46ᵇ</cite> (some eds. <he>תכפריני</he>).

senses.gloss: [to wipe out,] to forgive, atone; to procure forgiveness.
units: <cite ref="Yoma 5a:5">Yoma 5ᵃ</cite> <he>כאילו לא כ׳ וכפר</he> as if he (the priest) had not procured atonement (in the proper manner), although he has procured atonement (for the person concerned); <cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 14:10">Neg. XIV, 10</cite> <he>כ׳ ומעלין עליו כאילו לא כ׳</he> he has brought atonement, but it is accounted to the officiating priest as if he had not done so.

<cite ref="Berakhot 55a">Ber. 55ᵃ</cite> … <he>כל זמן מזבח מְכַפֵּר על וכ׳</he> as long as the Temple existed, the altar was the means of atonement for Israel, but now each man’s table must be the means of atonement (ref. to <cite ref="Ezekiel 41:22">Ez. XLI, 22</cite>). Tanḥ. Vayishl. 6 <he>כשם … מְכַפֶּרֶת וכ׳</he> as the altar brings atonement, so does she (the chaste wife) atone for her household.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 57a:3">Kidd. 57ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>מכשיר ומכפר</he>, v. <cite ref="K01324"><he>כָּשֵׁר</he> I</cite>; a. v. fr.—[<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 46b">Ab. Zar. 46ᵇ</cite>, v. supra].

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 18a">R. Hash. 18ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yevamot 105a:13-14">Yeb. 105ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="I Samuel 3:14">I Sam. III, 14</cite>) <he>בזבח … מִתְכַּפֵּר וכ׳</he> through sacrifice … it will not be expiated, but it may be so by the study of the Law.

<cite ref="Shevuot 12a:14">Shebu. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>אשם … שנִתְכַּפְּרוּ בעליו</he> an animal dedicated for a guilt-offering … whose owner has otherwise obtained atonement; (<cite ref="Mishnah Temurah 3:3">Tem. III, 3</cite> <he>שכִּפְּרוּ וכ׳</he> whose owner has procured atonement &c.).
<cite ref="Yoma 50b">Yoma 50ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <cite ref="K01046"><he>המִתְכַּפֵּר</he></cite> he for whose atonement the animal is dedicated.

<cite ref="Yoma 51b:2">Ib. 51ᵇ</cite> <he>שאין הצבור מִתְכַּפְּרִין בו</he> as the community is not to obtain forgiveness through it (the bullock); a. fr.—Y. Macc. II, 31ᵈ bot. <he>יעשה … ויִתְכַּפֶּר לו</he> let him repent and he shall be forgiven; Pesik. Shub. p. 158ᵇ; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 358">Yalk. Ez. 358</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 702">Yalk. Ps. 702</cite>. Tanḥ. T’rum. 8 <he>נתכ׳ להם</he> they were forgiven; a. fr.
